comparison: Perfect agreement. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers fully support the finding that Su(H) is phosphorylated at S269 upon wasp infestation (C3, C59, C60, C61). Both cite Figure 2B western blot data as convincing evidence.

Complete agreement. Both evaluations support the expression and localization data for Pkc53E in blood cells (C94, C95), based on Figure 8 imaging and RT-PCR data. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Divergent assessments of antibody quality (C58). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED noting cross-reactivity but acceptable validation. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting the antibody's 'insufficient' specificity and sensitivity prevented direct in vivo testing of Pkc53E-mediated phosphorylation.

Strong agreement. Both support the pharmacological data using PMA and staurosporine (C80-C88) showing PKC-mediated regulation of Su(H). OpenEval notes differential response of S269A mutants; peer reviewers accept the data without challenge.

Full agreement. Both evaluations support the ADP-Glo kinase assay data (C73, C74, C76, C77, C78) demonstrating substrate specificity and activation requirements for Pkc53E. Peer reviewers praise the biochemical approaches.

Strong agreement. Both support the genetic epistasis and co-immunoprecipitation data (C89-C93) showing Pkc53E-Su(H) interaction. Peer reviewers describe the epistatic data as 'convincing' and note the work 'convincingly shows' the interaction is critical.

Strong agreement. Both support the identification of Pkc53E as the kinase (C62, C63, C67, C68, C69, C72) through multiple approaches. Peer reviewers praise this as 'very nice' and 'well addressed in its entirety.'

Agreement with important caveat. Both support that Pkc53E mutants show compromised immune response (C96, C99, C100). However, peer review explicitly notes the confounding factor that reduced baseline hemocyte numbers (C97) may explain the phenotype rather than defective Notch downregulation. OpenEval acknowledges this complication but both mark as SUPPORTED.

Complete agreement on the observation. Both accept that Pkc53E mutants have constitutively reduced hemocyte numbers (C97). Peer review explicitly notes this as a potential confounding factor for interpreting immune defects.

Strong agreement on Notch activity regulation. Both support that Su(H)S269A mutants cannot properly downregulate Notch activity (C43, C44, C50, C51, C52). Peer review also includes lamellocyte and survival claims, calling the data 'convincing.'

Strong agreement on lamellocyte formation. Both support reduced lamellocyte formation in Su(H)S269A mutants (C47, C48, C49). OpenEval focuses specifically on lamellocyte markers; peer review groups this with broader immune phenotypes.

Strong agreement on survival phenotypes. Both support reduced survival of Su(H)S269A mutants upon wasp infestation (C5, C54, C55, C56, C57). Peer review groups survival data with other immune phenotypes in their comprehensive assessment.

OpenEval supports claims about phosphorylation mechanism and DNA binding inhibition (C4, C35, C115) based on prior work and current functional data. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found for these mechanistic claims.
OpenEval supports claims about Su(H)'s dual role in homeostasis and stress response (C38, C40, C110, C116). No specific peer review evaluation addresses these broader functional claims.

OpenEval supports the main integrated conclusions (C11, C42, C154) synthesizing multiple lines of evidence. Peer reviewers affirm overall conclusions but don't provide a separate evaluation specifically for these summary claims.
OpenEval supports genetic epistasis between Notch and Su(H) (C156, C157) based on Figure 1 supplement data. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found for these control experiments.

OpenEval supports hemocyte count data showing specificity to cell type composition (C45, C158, C159). No corresponding specific peer review evaluation, though related to concerns about baseline hemocyte numbers in other contexts.
OpenEval supports validation of Pkc53E null allele (C161) based on RT-PCR data. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found for this technical validation.

OpenEval marks evolutionary conservation claims (C151, C152, C153, C155) as UNCERTAIN, noting functional significance in mammals requires validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these speculative claims.
OpenEval supports observation about Pkc53EEDDD activity (C79) while noting speculation about causes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this technical observation.

OpenEval supports extensive background/context claims (C1, C2, C12-C150, C160) from literature. These represent established knowledge rather than novel findings, so peer reviewers don't separately evaluate them.
